text: APC/C, with cofactor Cdh1, targets cell-cycle proteins for degradation in late mitosis and G1. Cdh1-null embryos die at E9.5–E10.5 from trophoblast endoreduplication defects and placental malfunction; placental Cdh1 expression rescues lethality. Cdh1-deficient cells proliferate poorly and accumulate numeric and structural chromosomal aberrations, so Cdh1 maintains genomic stability. Cdh1 heterozygotes show increased spontaneous tumour susceptibility, indicating haploinsufficient tumour suppression, plus behavioural defects tied to neural stem-cell proliferation. Separately, ribosomal protein heterozygote mice restoring normal protein synthesis in Emu-Myc/+ mice suppressed Myc oncogenicity: Myc-driven protein synthesis increases cell size and accelerates cell-cycle progression independently of transcriptional targets, and normal synthesis lets programmed cell death eliminate precancerous cells. Aberrant cap-dependent translation impairs the IRES-dependent translational switch needed for mitosis, reducing IRES-dependent Cdk11 (Cdc2l/PITSLRE), causing cytokinesis defects, centrosome amplification and genome instability in Emu-Myc/+ mice—reversed by restoring translational control.
